clue.text: Almost the end of Brown being collared by stupid arse and bloody heartless Trust

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement is a muddled one, so the word that follows is jumbled
a collar goes round a neck, so the jumbled word wraps round the single selected letter

parts.note: the four letters rearranged

indicators.note: not quite the final letter of the word, so the one just before the last is taken

parts.note: the next-to-last letter of Brown

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outside letters of the following word survive

parts.note: the first and last letters of bloody

explanation.surface: A furious rant about Gordon Brown being manhandled, ending in a cry about trust.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown reads as Gordon Brown, the Prime Minister, but it is only a word to take a letter from; 'bloody' is British mild swearing used here for its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear by something is to have complete confidence in it, so the phrasal verb means to put faith in it.

clue.text: Tory grandee united — leader cut out tongue

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and cutting it out drops that letter from the grandee's name

parts.note: Douglas Hurd, Conservative Foreign Secretary and party elder
U is the standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A senior Tory and his party unite in silencing someone, with the leader cutting out a tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Hurd was a senior Conservative minister in the Thatcher and Major governments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old word for a language, and Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

clue.text: Dope: lump given to Springer

parts.note: a clod is a lump of earth
something that springs is a hopper

explanation.surface: A drug-smuggling scene: a lump of dope handed to a man called Springer, perhaps the TV host.
explanation.walkthrough: Springer reads like a surname but just means one who springs or hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, oafish person, and a dope is a stupid one, so both are insults for a dolt.

clue.text: Talk of leak being suppressed by school

to take a leak is slang for to urinate

explanation.surface: Gossip about a scandalous leak that a school is trying to hush up.
explanation.walkthrough: The leak looks like a news leak, but it is the toilet sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech is a formal talk given to an audience, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Dick stands on head to screw

indicators.note: turning upside down in a down entry flips the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A man performs a headstand as a prelude to sex.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, standing on its head puts the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for the penis, and also for a fool.

clue.text: Hawking's source of IC shit? Born awkward

indicators.note: awkward letters are badly arranged, signalling that they must be rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A crude question about where Stephen Hawking got some of his science.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawking looks like the physicist, but here it is hawking in the sense of clearing the throat noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronchitis, inflammation of the airways, makes a sufferer cough up phlegm, which is what hawking means.

clue.text: Ex-PM has cracked! About to give up!

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the word before it is put back in a new order
about means around, so the broken word goes round the phrase that follows

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
to quit is to give up

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister has had a breakdown and is about to throw in the towel.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was the Liberal Prime Minister of Britain from 1908 to 1916, so a former holder of the office.

clue.text: From Dewar, bleeding twitter

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the words that follow, lying across them

parts.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A bloodied politician, perhaps Donald Dewar, posts a sweary message on Twitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bleeding is the British mild swear word, but it is just carrying letters; Dewar is a whisky brand and a Scottish politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To twitter is to chirp like a bird, and warbling is a bird's trilling song, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Uranium applied to member? Member's revolting!

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
pin is slang for leg, a limb or member
another limb, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at a radioactive substance being rubbed on a penis.
explanation.walkthrough: Member suggests the rude sense but means a limb each time; revolting means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in arms is an idiom for angry and protesting, which is close to the rebellious sense of revolting.

clue.text: Sailor (vulgar one) Ball gets piles

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
'un is the dialect or vulgar way of saying one
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A crude sailor named Ball suffers from haemorrhoids.
explanation.walkthrough: Piles reads as the medical complaint but means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Piles of something means a great quantity of it, which is what an abundance is.

clue.text: US agency sending people up over length of organ

parts.note: the American space agency, which launches astronauts
L is the standard abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A space agency launching astronauts somehow above an organ's length.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, NASA written over L puts it first; the organ is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal is the adjective for the nose, so it means belonging to that particular organ of the body.

clue.text: Dubya not quiet about "insect" African people

indicators.note: about means around, so what is left of the name wraps around the insect
not means without, so the quiet signal is removed from the president's name

parts.note: Dubya is the nickname of George W. Bush
sh is the call for quiet
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: George W. Bush loudly and offensively calling Africans insects.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large group of peoples across central and southern Africa sharing related languages.

clue.text: Infantile, shit bank robber is $1000 down without a robbery

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name sits around the robbery
being down by an amount means short of it, so that sum is taken out of the robber's name

parts.note: Ronnie Biggs, the Great Train Robber
a grand, G, is a thousand
a job is criminal slang for a robbery

explanation.surface: A sneering verdict on a bank robber who is broke because he never pulled off a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Biggs was a famous British robber of the 1963 Great Train Robbery; drop one G from his name and put JOB inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Big jobs is nursery language for defecation, so it is the infantile word for that bodily function.

clue.text: Ooh-er, organ's made manky by this?

definitions.text: Ooh-er, organ's made manky by this?

indicators.note: something made manky has been spoiled and messed about, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A comic shriek of alarm at a diseased private part.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition; manky is British slang for dirty or rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: This sexually transmitted infection affects the genitals, so it is what makes that organ diseased.

clue.text: Smitten, sporting an erection — success!

parts.note: slang for being aroused
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A lovestruck man is visibly aroused and counts it a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Smitten looks like love-struck but is taken in its literal sense of struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten literally means struck heavily, and hard-hit means badly affected by a blow.

clue.text: Queen's common consort: difficult profession

parts.note: rough means hard or difficult
a trade is a line of work

explanation.surface: Being the Queen's commoner husband is a hard job.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is gay slang for an effeminate gay man, not the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough trade is slang for a working-class or tough male sexual partner, which suits a common consort.

clue.text: 'Pencil' not up, sadly? Could be the tabloid's one is too low

definitions.text: the tabloid's one is too low
definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a strict synonym

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are out of order

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A limp 'pencil' is a sad sight, perhaps because the paper has too few topless pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is mocking tabloids that judge their own worth by how much bare flesh they print, as with the Sun's Page Three.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid that thinks it needs more topless photos would be complaining about its tally of exposed breasts.

clue.text: Half a month in jail to produce this sort of music?

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the other half being thrown away

parts.note: June is a month; July would work just as well

explanation.surface: Two weeks in prison is enough to make someone start playing a particular kind of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajun music is the folk style of the French-descended people of Louisiana, so it names a genre.

clue.text: Stage bloke on second is pissed

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An actor on stage for the second act is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed here is British slang for drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for very drunk, so drunk that one cannot stand, a synonym of pissed.

clue.text: Local indicator of sinning getting out of control

indicators.note: letters out of control run wild and lose their order, so they must be reordered

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood sign that moral decay has run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Local is British slang for one's nearby pub, which is why its sign is an indicator of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The board hung outside a pub shows its name, so it signals where the nearest boozer is.

clue.text: Heard rumour: "time lost vibrating part of organ"

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so those letters are removed from the phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane that vibrates when sound waves reach the ear, the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Brooding party leader needs quick surgery internally

explanation.walkthrough: Menzies Campbell (pronounced Ming-is) was widely called Ming in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Moping and brooding both describe sulking in a gloomy, listless way, so the participles are synonyms.

clue.text: One of Brown's men takes issue but Bush's convenience comes first

explanation.walkthrough: Alan Johnson served in Gordon Brown's cabinet; a convenience is a British word for a public toilet.

clue.text: Bovril enema involves needle
